Title: Uncertainty-aware future trajectory prediction and collision risk assessment for moving objects in manufacturing workspaces
Affiliations: Department of Applied Artificial Intelligence, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Seoul, South Korea
Authors with affiliations: Hong M.J., Department of Applied Artificial Intelligence, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Seoul, South Korea; Kim B.S., Department of Applied Artificial Intelligence, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Seoul, South Korea
Abstract: This study proposes a deep learning framework for uncertainty-aware trajectory prediction and collision risk assessment in industrial environments. While uncertainty prediction methods exist, integrating them into an efficient, real-time industrial safety framework remains a challenge. Our framework addresses this gap by employing a Temporal Self-Attention Bi-LSTM model with Lower–Upper Bound Estimation (LUBE) to generate prediction intervals. Collision risk is then assessed using an Intersection over Union (IoU) metric on these intervals. To improve computational efficiency in multi-agent scenarios, the framework uses KNN-based candidate pairing, while a proximity-based dynamic IoU threshold provides adaptive risk sensitivity. Experiments on a Unity-based digital twin dataset validate our model's architecture through ablation studies. Furthermore, a real-world accident CCTV case study provides preliminary evidence of the framework’s feasibility for preemptive collision prediction. The results suggest the potential applicability of the framework for uncertainty-aware collision risk assessment in industrial environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: An Explainable Digital Twin Framework for Integrating Regenerative Agriculture, Climate-Resilient Food Systems, and Sustainable Nutrition

Abstract: Sustainable agricultural management faces growing challenges from climate change, water scarcity, energy constraints, soil degradation, and the need to ensure both food production and nutritional security. This study proposes an integrated computational framework combining a Global Agricultural Foundation Representation Model (GAFRM), Self-Evolving Explainable Digital Twin (SEDT), Self-Evolving Evolutionary Foundation Optimizer (SEEFO), and an enhanced Green Regenerative Agriculture Sustainability Index (GRASI). The framework operationalizes the food–water–energy–carbon–nutrition (FWEC-N) nexus by explicitly incorporating crop micronutrient density into the agricultural decision architecture and modeling its relationship with regenerative practices such as cover cropping, biochar application, and zero tillage. Using multi-source global datasets, GAFRM learns transferable agricultural representations, SEDT enables adaptive prediction under climate uncertainty, and SEEFO performs five-objective optimization of agricultural productivity, irrigation water use, energy demand, net carbon balance, and overall sustainability, while nutritional quality is evaluated through the MODI outcome indicator. The enhanced GRASI further evaluates nutrient output, soil restoration, carbon storage, and climate resilience within a unified sustainability framework. The framework was evaluated using a global agricultural dataset covering approximately 60 representative countries across six continents and 15 climate zones over the 2000–2026 period. SEDT achieved an RMSE of 3.18, MAE of 2.29, R2 of 0.972, and NSE of 0.968, while SEEFO achieved the highest Hypervolume (0.956) and the lowest GD (0.028), IGD (0.039), and Spread (0.162) among the benchmark optimization algorithms. The observed performance differences were statistically significant according to the Wilcoxon signed-rank and Friedman tests (p < 0.05). The findings indicate that integrating nutritional quality with resource efficiency, carbon balance, soil regeneration, and climate resilience provides a more comprehensive basis for evaluating regenerative agricultural strategies. The architecture establishes a fully transparent, explainable decision-support environment through explainable AI (XAI) feature attributions, bridging the gap between digital precision farming, regenerative ecosystem restoration, and sustainable human nutrition under increasing environmental uncertainty. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: AI-driven non-destructive inspection in smart manufacturing: A review of techniques for structural integrity and process quality enhancement
Source title: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part B: Journal of Engineering Manufacture
Affiliations: Centre for Quality Assurance and Non Destructive Evaluation, Sathyabama Institute of Science Technology, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India
Authors with affiliations: Kumar S., Centre for Quality Assurance and Non Destructive Evaluation, Sathyabama Institute of Science Technology, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India
Abstract: Non-Destructive Evaluation (NDE) is essential for ensuring product quality, structural integrity, and process reliability in modern manufacturing without disrupting production. However, conventional NDE methods often involve operator-dependent interpretation, large and heterogeneous datasets, and limited integration with automated manufacturing systems. Machine Learning (ML) has increasingly transformed NDE into an intelligent, data-driven approach by enabling automated defect detection, classification, segmentation, characterization, and real-time decision-making. This paper presents a comprehensive review of ML applications across major NDE modalities, including Ultrasonic Testing (UT), Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT), Radiographic Testing (RT), Infrared Thermography (IRT), Acoustic Emission (AE), Eddy Current Testing (ECT), and vision-based inspection, with emphasis on manufacturing quality assurance. Classical ML techniques, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, k-Nearest Neighbors, and Gaussian Mixture Models, are reviewed alongside deep-learning architectures such as Convolutional Neural Networks, U-Net, CNN–LSTM, and transformer-based models. The review critically examines challenges related to limited and imbalanced datasets, domain generalization, interpretability, computational requirements, uncertainty, and standardization. Emerging directions, including multimodal data fusion, physics-informed ML, digital twins, edge AI, autonomous inspection, and explainable AI, are discussed as key enablers for reliable and adaptive NDE systems. Overall, ML-driven NDE provides a pathway toward intelligent, predictive, and increasingly autonomous quality assurance aligned with Industry 4.0 and sustainable manufacturing. © IMechE 2026

Abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for improving the performance, robustness, and efficiency of electrical machine drive systems. Among AI-based approaches, fuzzy logic control (FLC) has attracted considerable attention because of its ability to handle nonlinear dynamics, parameter uncertainties, and external disturbances without relying on an accurate mathematical model. This review systematically examines FLC-based control strategies for electrical machine drives, with particular emphasis on induction motors, switched reluctance motors, permanent-magnet synchronous motors, synchronous reluctance motors, and brushless DC motors. The review follows the PRISMA 2020 framework, and the selected studies are analyzed according to machine type, FLC architecture, control strategy, optimization method, implementation platform, and validation approach. The reviewed evidence indicates that FLC-based strategies can improve dynamic response, tracking accuracy, robustness, and torque regulation under the specific conditions reported in the literature. Hybrid approaches combining FLC with field-oriented control, direct torque control, sliding-mode control, model predictive control, neural networks, ANFIS, and optimization algorithms provide additional opportunities for adaptation and parameter tuning. However, the reported performance is strongly dependent on machine topology, controller architecture, tuning methodology, computational requirements, and validation platform. The review also identifies important limitations, including the lack of standardized benchmarking, computational complexity, dependence on expert knowledge, and limited HIL and experimental validation of several advanced approaches. Emerging directions include Type-2 and higher-order fuzzy systems, neuro-fuzzy and hybrid AI controllers, data-driven optimization, digital-twin-assisted control, edge computing, and hardware-oriented implementation. The objective of this review is to provide a structured and critical synthesis of the existing evidence, clarify the evolution and practical applicability of AI-driven FLC approaches, and identify research priorities for reliable, computationally efficient, and experimentally validated electrical machine control. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Living Lab: cooperative, predictive and resilient AI-driven infrastructure
Source title: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers: Municipal Engineer
Affiliations: Connected Urban Mobility Learning Traffic Infrastructure, Aschaffenburg University of Applied Science, Aschaffenburg, Germany
Authors with affiliations: Weidl G., Connected Urban Mobility Learning Traffic Infrastructure, Aschaffenburg University of Applied Science, Aschaffenburg, Germany; Talluri K.K., Connected Urban Mobility Learning Traffic Infrastructure, Aschaffenburg University of Applied Science, Aschaffenburg, Germany
Abstract: Urban mobility systems continued to be strained due to traffic disturbances, including congestion, accidents, and emissions, resulting in significant financial, economic, and safety losses. Especially for stochastic disruptions or unforeseen events, such as traffic anomalies caused by various traffic disturbances, accidents and severe weather conditions, traditional traffic management systems and signal controls struggle to cope. To overcome these limitations, the transport ecosystem should transform the infrastructure to involve more intelligent, predictive, and cooperative participants. This work highlights several research efforts and complementary modules developed at TH Aschaffenburg over the past few years. An explainable and accident-aware congestion prediction framework is designed using a Bayesian network, followed by a multi-class fog modelling for weather-aware, robust perception. Moreover, ongoing research on the development and integration of reinforcement learning-based adaptive traffic signal control for traffic optimisation under uncertainty, a vehicle-to-everything-ready architecture for cooperative vehicle-infrastructure interaction, and the development of a digital twin framework for achieving a robust and reliable strategy through rigorous testing and validation is highlighted. Although these modules are studied individually, TH Aschaffenburg’s LiDAR-equipped City Mobility Living Lab facilitates the creation of an artificial intelligence-driven platform to unify, validate, and extend this research within real-world settings. © 2026 Emerald Publishing Limited

Title: PerioTwin-DeltaCRED: a validation-aware physiological digital twin for longitudinal periodontal treatment response prediction
Affiliations: Department of Periodontics, Saveetha Dental College and Hospitals, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences (SIMATS), Chennai, India
Authors with affiliations: Yadalam P.K., Department of Periodontics, Saveetha Dental College and Hospitals, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences (SIMATS), Chennai, India
Abstract: Background – Predicting individual periodontal treatment response remains clinically unresolved. Existing machine-learning models are predominantly cross-sectional, lack a longitudinal response-vector design, and are rarely evaluated within validation-aware digital-twin frameworks that capture multidimensional credibility rather than single-endpoint discrimination alone. This study aimed to develop and evaluate PerioTwin-DeltaCRED, a validation-aware periodontal digital twin that models treatment response as a longitudinal PPD and CAL response vector, and to benchmark classical and quantum machine-learning engines against that framework. Methods – Five hundred patients with Stage II-IV periodontitis were retrospectively assembled from the Saveetha DIAS system; treatment was observational, involving either scaling and root planing alone or with low-level laser therapy. A stratified 60:20:20 split (training n=300, validation n=100, test n=100) was used for all models, using only baseline predictors—follow-up measurements and outcome variables were excluded to prevent leakage. Classical learners (logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting) were benchmarked for poor-response classification, PPD reduction, CAL gain, and residual deep-pocket risk. Three quantum architectures—VQC-Pauli, Data Re-Uploading VQC (DRU-VQC), and QSVC—along with a hybrid quantum–classical stack, were evaluated as exploratory engines; six principal components (83.6% of variance) were angle-encoded into six-qubit circuits. Hyperparameters were optimized by Optuna on the validation set, with the test set withheld until final assessment. Uncertainty was estimated by bootstrap resampling, and the Delta-PTFI summarized credibility. Results – Classical logistic regression was the strongest poor-response model (test AUROC 0.69, 95% CI 0.59–0.80; sensitivity 0.54, specificity 0.75), with random forest comparable (AUROC 0.68) and providing the best residual deep-pocket discrimination (AUROC 0.76). Continuous responses were predicted with modest error (PPD-reduction mean absolute error 0.37 mm; CAL-gain 0.31 mm); against observed changes of 1.20 ± 0.46 mm and 0.78 ± 0.36 mm, these errors were equivalent to an intercept-only baseline. Baseline CAL and periodontal stage were the dominant and most stable predictors (mean top-5 stability 0.75), and a two-variable model using stage and baseline CAL alone matched the full model (AUROC 0.71 versus 0.69). An exploratory composite credibility index (Delta-PTFI) was 0.62, falling to 0.25 when its continuous-outcome components were anchored to an intercept-only reference. No quantum architecture surpassed classical learning: the data re-uploading classifier (DRU-VQC) was the best quantum model (test AUROC 0.63), followed by the hybrid stack (0.60), VQC-Pauli (0.46), and QSVC (0.40). Classical learners restricted to the same six principal components reached AUROC 0.58–0.66, and the best of them (random forest, 0.66) still exceeded every quantum model. Conclusion – PerioTwin-DeltaCRED provides a validation-aware digital twin for periodontal treatment response, assessing calibration, fidelity, response stability, and credibility index instead of just discrimination. Classical models outperformed, and quantum architectures like DRU-VQC showed no advantage in noiseless six-qubit tests. This is among the first studies embedding and benchmarking quantum machine learning in a periodontal digital twin; more validation and noise testing is needed before clinical use. Abstract: The modeling of new power systems is aided by technical support of algorithms and Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems. In regards to renewable energy coupled to multi-constraint systems, operation of the systems is subject to significant uncertainty and dynamically complex behavior, creating challenges for traditional methods of planning systems. To resolve these challenges, the authors of this paper present a new approach to planning power systems: a constraint-based digital twin collaborative planning architecture. This sensor architecture, with the physical-virtual mapping and multi-dimensional feature modeling, can achieve real-time perception and prediction of the state of the system, and with the hierarchical optimization and distributed collaborative algorithms, it may be possible to achieve and cross-level decision-collaborative mechanisms. In the comparative tests conducted in this study, this method achieved the best results in terms of power loss, violations of system operation constraints, system operational renewable energy absorption, while providing the system with optimal operational performance, minimizing processing time and overcoming instabilities of the system. This architecture is promising for the flexible planning and intelligent optimization to complex power systems. © 2026 The Authors.

Abstract: The large-scale integration of wind and solar power is essential for power-sector decarbonization, but their variability creates persistent challenges for forecasting, reserve allocation, storage scheduling, curtailment, and emission-aware operation. This review synthesizes recent advances in statistical, deep-learning, transformer, foundation-model, probabilistic, and physics-informed renewable forecasting, with emphasis on physical consistency, uncertainty, computational requirements, real-time applicability, and system-level operational value. We propose the Physics-Informed Large Model Carbon-Aware (PILM-CA) framework, a conceptual architecture linking physical renewable dynamics, physics-informed large-model forecasting, grid-operational decision support, and carbon-aware optimization. Unlike accuracy-centric forecasting frameworks, PILM-CA explicitly represents the pathway through which forecast uncertainty can affect commitment, reserves, storage, fossil backup, curtailment, and consequent carbon intensity. Published evidence indicates that these effects are system-dependent rather than universal; therefore, the framework distinguishes evidence-supported components from conceptual cross-layer relationships requiring operational validation. Probabilistic forecasting metrics, extreme-event resilience, digital-twin deployment, technology readiness, and climate adaptation are also critically examined. The review identifies research priorities for scalable, physically coherent, uncertainty-aware forecasting that supports both decarbonization and resilience in high-renewable power systems. © 2026 The Authors

Abstract: In the context of digital transformation and the EU Green Deal, machine vision systems (MVSs) are emerging as key technologies for automated inspection, quality control, and precision measurement across industries such as aeronautics, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, electronics, and semiconductors. Despite their growing adoption, MVSs often lack traceability and standardised calibration methods, making their deployment in manufacturing indispensable for ensuring accuracy and reliability. The DI-Vision project tackles these challenges by developing traceable material standards with prismatic and complex geometries, better representing real-world industrial surfaces. The project also advances the use of Digital Twins (DTs) to enable robust uncertainty evaluations and accurate MVS modelling. Additionally, dense-image matching algorithms, along with defect detection classifiers and analysis tools, aiming at enhancing the reliability of industrial inspections are proposed. To validate these developments, DI-Vision will investigate industrial case studies across 13 applications, spanning multiple sectors. The project will also deliver Good Practice Guides (GPGs) and establish a measurement infrastructure through collaboration with European Metrology Networks (EMNs) MathMet, TraceLabMed, AdvManu, as well as standards organisations (ISO/TC213, ASTM) and key industrial stakeholders. By providing traceable solutions, DI-Vision will drive advancements in industrial automation and precision manufacturing, ensuring greater reliability and efficiency across diverse sectors. © 2025 Renishaw plc. Title: AI-Driven Architectural Space Reconstruction and Digital Twin Coordination for Urban Renewal Scenarios
Affiliations: College of Architecture and Urban Planning, Changchun University of Architecture and Civil Engineering, Jilin, Changchun, 130607, China
Authors with affiliations: Wei Y., College of Architecture and Urban Planning, Changchun University of Architecture and Civil Engineering, Jilin, Changchun, 130607, China; Lv G., College of Architecture and Urban Planning, Changchun University of Architecture and Civil Engineering, Jilin, Changchun, 130607, China
Abstract: Urban renewal requires reliable digital representations of existing architectural spaces to support spatial diagnosis, compliance checking, and lifecycle updating. Although AI-based reconstruction and digital twin technologies have advanced rapidly, existing approaches often remain weakly connected: reconstruction methods mainly optimize geometric or semantic accuracy, while digital twin systems frequently depend on static or manually verified spatial inputs. To address this limitation, this study proposes an AI-driven architectural space reconstruction and digital twin coordination framework for urban renewal scenarios. The framework integrates multi-source spatial data, including RGB-D images, point clouds, BIM/IFC information, GIS context, and renewal constraints. It further introduces a renewal-constraint graph, a twin-guided reconstruction module, and an uncertainty-aware synchronization mechanism to improve constraint consistency and reduce unreliable twin updates. Experiments were conducted on ScanNet, Matterport3D, and BuildingNet, with five repeated trials. Compared with NeuralRecon, the proposed method improves mIoU from 67.6% to 69.1%, reduces the constraint violation rate from 13.6% to 11.8%, and decreases synchronization latency from 1.12 s to 0.98 s. However, NeuralRecon still performs slightly better in Chamfer Distance and reconstruction completeness. These results suggest that the proposed framework provides limited but consistent gains in renewal-related indicators, especially compliance control and digital twin update reliability. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Mechanobiology-aware autonomous antifouling interfaces: multimodal sensing, adaptive actuation, and closed-loop biofouling control
Affiliations: Department of Chemistry, Yeungnam University, Gyeongsan, South Korea; Department of Life Sciences, Yeungnam University, Gyeongsan, South Korea
Authors with affiliations: Akhtar M.S., Department of Chemistry, Yeungnam University, Gyeongsan, South Korea; Zaman W., Department of Life Sciences, Yeungnam University, Gyeongsan, South Korea
Abstract: Biofouling is a dynamic, spatially heterogeneous, and history-dependent interfacial process, whereas most control strategies remain static or calendar-based. This mismatch can cause unnecessary chemical and energy use, delayed intervention, coating damage, and incomplete recovery. This critical review develops a mechanobiology-aware framework for autonomous antifouling interfaces that detect a fouling-relevant signal, estimate latent interfacial state, select a bounded action, actuate locally, and verify recovery. It links conditioning-film ageing, bacterial surface sensing, cyclic di-GMP-mediated commitment, extracellular polymeric substance assembly, collective mechanics, transport limitation, community interactions, and dispersal to optical, electrochemical, acoustic, mechanical, and molecular sensing. Electrochemical, optical, thermal, acoustic, hydrodynamic, topographic, hydrated or liquid-infused, enzymatic, and quorum-interference actuation are evaluated in relation to target state and failure mode. Passive resistance, pre-programmed responsiveness, and genuine closed-loop operation are distinguished explicitly. The proposed architecture treats the fouled interface as a partially observed system in which multimodal measurements support an uncertainty-aware state estimate, a constrained policy selects the least harmful action likely to succeed, and post-action sensing verifies biological and functional recovery. Reduced digital-twin models are positioned as decision-support tools rather than as established universal solutions. Key deployment requirements include calibration transfer, sensor self-fouling, latency, material ageing, detached-biomass capture, release accounting, safe fallback, and direct comparison with the identical actuator operated open-loop. © 2026 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

Abstract: Aerospace welding is moving beyond preset-parameter automation toward process-integrated quality assurance. In this setting, material response, process observability, adaptive action, and traceable evidence must operate as coordinated functions rather than as separate technologies. This review applies a reproducible structured search covering January 2000 to July 2026, supplemented by earlier landmark sources, and classifies the literature as direct aerospace demonstration, transferable non-aerospace evidence, or conceptual enabling technology. High-strength aluminum alloys, titanium alloys, nickel-based superalloys, thermoplastic composites, and dissimilar joints are examined alongside friction stir, high-energy-beam, hybrid, and composite welding routes. The analysis then addresses one-, two-, and three-dimensional sensing, multimodal spatiotemporal alignment, defect and performance prediction, adaptive control, and digital-twin architectures. Evidence is comparatively mature for local sensing, defect recognition, and offline optimization. By contrast, validation remains limited for out-of-distribution reliability, physics-constrained transfer across materials and processes, millisecond-scale virtual-real closure, and certification-grade links between process signatures and residual strength or fatigue life. The proposed roadmap assigns high-fidelity models to offline learning and validation, reduced-order or surrogate models to online state estimation, and uncertainty-aware decisions to auditable safety limits. This synthesis defines the conditions required for intelligent welding to progress toward deployable, quality-assured closed-loop manufacturing of aerospace structures. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd on behalf of The Society of Manufacturing Engineers.

Abstract: The increasing penetration of variable solar and wind generation requires flexible resources capable of improving energy balancing, reliability, and renewable energy utilization. This review critically assesses biofuel-integrated hybrid energy systems as complementary architectures for renewable energy integration, connecting system configuration, energy conversion efficiency, storage and dispatch, intelligent control, environmental performance, and scalability. A critical narrative and integrative approach was applied using literature retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science, and organized across solar–bioenergy, wind–bioenergy, multi-source, storage-supported, microgrid, and multi-energy configurations. The evidence indicates that biomass-derived fuels can provide dispatchable and storable renewable energy that complements variable generation and supports decentralized and multi-energy applications. However, no architecture is universally superior, and greater hybridization does not inherently result in higher thermodynamic efficiency. Performance depends strongly on resource complementarity, feedstock availability and quality, conversion pathways, storage requirements, and operating strategy. Advanced energy management, model predictive control, machine learning, and digital twins can improve system coordination, although much of the available evidence remains simulation-based or limited in experimental scale. Environmental benefits are likewise pathway- and boundary-dependent, particularly when avoided emissions, coproduct allocation, infrastructure, and feedstock supply chains are considered. Overall, biofuel-integrated hybrid systems represent an application-dependent flexibility option rather than a universally optimal solution; future progress requires dynamic uncertainty-aware modeling, harmonized techno-economic and life-cycle assessment, and greater pilot- and industrial-scale validation. © 2026 by the authors.

Abstract: Accurate battery state-of-health (SOH) estimation is essential for reliable electric vehicle operation. This paper presents a unified digital twin framework that combines attention-based sequence modeling with physics-guided learning for robust SOH prediction. A Kalman filter-based refinement is incorporated to improve tracking stability under nonlinear degradation. The framework also includes visualization and uncertainty analysis to enhance interpretability. Experimental results on NASA lithium-ion battery datasets (B0033, B0034, and B0036) demonstrate improved prediction accuracy, stability, and cross-battery generalization compared to conventional methods. A real-time AI dashboard further validates its practical applicability for monitoring, remaining useful life estimation, and risk-aware decision-making. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Uncertainty-Aware 3D Generative Scene Completion for Industrial Digital Twin Initialization under Occlusion
Affiliations: Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47906, IN, United States
Authors with affiliations: Woo S., Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47906, IN, United States; Woo S.H., Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47906, IN, United States; Son Y.-J., Edwardson School of Industrial Engineering, Purdue University, West Lafayette, 47906, IN, United States
Abstract: Digital twin (DT) environment model initialization and updates are increasingly essential for manufacturing commissioning, reconfiguration, and robot planning, yet accurate 3D DT creation remains a major bottleneck: current practice often requires months of manual CAD modeling, delaying ramp-up after new installations or layout changes. Although autonomous mobile robots can scan facilities rapidly, industrial scenes exhibit severe occlusions and sensing gaps, which makes DT initialization under partial observability unreliable when missing structure is completed deterministically without representing uncertainty. We propose a confidence-guided, uncertainty-aware hierarchical scene completion framework that accelerates DT initialization while explicitly quantifying the unknown. First, we derive a per-voxel confidence signal from truncated signed distance fields (TSDF) fusion statistics (integration weights) and partition the map into local blocks. Unlike prior completion pipelines that uniformly hallucinate missing regions, we select only structurally uncertain blocks for generative inference and preserve well-observed regions unchanged. This design improves computational efficiency and prevents overwriting trusted geometry. Second, we develop a 3-level hierarchical Variational Autoencoder (VAE) for volumetric completion with multi-scale latent variables and a dual-head encoder-decoder that jointly predicts TSDF geometry and semantic labels. The probabilistic formulation yields calibrated per-voxel uncertainty via latent sampling and uncertainty propagation across scales. Experiments on the ScanNet dataset under 60% sparsity reveal that our method achieves 73.6% occupied Intersection over Union (IoU) and 85.5% semantic mean IoU, while substantially improving performance in truly unobserved space (74.5% IoU on unobserved voxels versus 9.11% for a deterministic method). Overall, our selective probabilistic completion provides competitive reconstruction quality and practical uncertainty estimates for rapid DT deployment in occluded industrial environments. © (2026) by Institute of Industrial & Systems Engineers (IISE) All rights reserved.

Abstract: The growing penetration of wind-solar hybrid renewable energy systems provides great operation uncertainty with stochastic wind speed, fluctuating solar irradiance and dynamic load demand. Conventional deterministic management operations of energy are not suitable for uncertainty-aware optimization and adaptive real-time operation and control. This paper proposes a Probabilistic Agentic AI-based Digital Twin intelligent and resilient operation of wind-solar hybrid energy systems. The proposed approach combines Bayesian probabilistic forecasting for modelling the environmental uncertainty and a multi-agent reinforcement learning-based control mechanism for the autonomous decision making. A real time digital twin layer aligns the physical and virtual replicas of physical assets to support predictive optimization and implementation of closed loop energy management. The goal of the optimization is to minimize costs of operating systems, unbalance and energy curtailment, given the constraints of uncertainty, and ensure the stability of the system. Extensive simulations are performed using realistic meteorological databases in order to test the forecasting accuracy and operation efficiency. Results prove that the proposed framework has improved reliability of prediction, less operation cost, and better stability of the electricity grid than deterministic LSTM-based and the conventional energy management approaches. Proposed architecture is a solution to the next generation issues in intelligent renewable microgrids and sustainable energy infrastructures in a reliable and scalable way, with an uncertainty-aware solution. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The complexity of today's modern waste management systems is rising due to the sustainable development of the circular economy and sustainability mandates, demanding decision framework integrating beyond conventional cost–benefit approach. Based on this, a hybrid model that combines the thermodynamic performance analysis, the lifecycle assessment, and the fuzzy multicriteria decision-making is proposed to suggest the recovery pathways in circular waste systems. The model provides the economic and environmental evaluation model incorporating fuzzy logic to address the uncertainties in economic and environmental evaluations in system boundaries, stakeholder preferences, and data variations. An architecture that integrates the energy efficiency metrics with the socioeconomic and lifecycle impact criteria is developed as a multilayering architecture. The framework is demonstrated to provide better accuracy and insight for decision-making on waste recovery policy alternatives and on siting and operating waste landfills or recovery facilities. Finally, the chapter summarizes barriers referring to implementation, policy implications, and prospects for future research about artificial intelligence– enhanced fuzzy systems and digital twins in relation to sustainable waste management. © 2026 Scrivener Publishing LLC.

Abstract: This work presents a digital twin framework for angular error compensation in a high-precision rotary table. The approach exploits continuous interaction between the physical rotary table and its virtual counterpart, where the physical system provides real-time measurements from a dual encoder, thermal probes, and capacitive sensors representative of the actual operating state. These measurements are fused in a particle-filter-based data assimilation module. The virtual rotary table is continuously updated and incorporates three complementary models: a geometrical error model, a thermal drift model, and sensor error models. By synchronizing the virtual entity with the physical system, the framework estimates the true angular position and delivers a corrected angle in real time. This corrected angle is used for metrological evaluation or fed back into the control loop. © 2026 EUSPEN. All Rights Reserved.

Abstract: Probabilistic digital twins are increasingly explored for continuous and personalized healthcare monitoring in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments. However, existing systems largely rely on fixed thresholds and deterministic rules that fail under noisy or incomplete data and contribute to alert fatigue. This paper presents a probabilistic digital twin framework that estimates latent ICU health states from physiological signals through a Bayesian Hidden Markov Model, with a behavioral modality integrated as an architectural extension demonstrated on a cross-dataset cohort, maintaining an online belief state for continuous, uncertainty-aware health status estimation. Evaluated on 64,691 intensive care unit (ICU) patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) dataset across 9,890,935 observation windows, the framework achieves an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.687, competitive with a supervised logistic regression baseline (AUC=0.740), with a median lead-time of 12.0 hours before vasopressor onset and 3.13 days before in-hospital death. Age-adjusted belief-state initialization personalizes risk estimation per patient, while a glass-box changebased attribution layer provides per-window clinical explanations without post-hoc approximation. A parameter sweep identifies conservative state transitions as the optimal operating point, maintaining a 14.7% false alarm rate. The framework offers a probabilistic and explainable monitoring approach suitable for Healthcare 5.0 applications. © 2026 University of Split, FESB.

Abstract: ［Objective］ In response to the pressing need for intelligent transformation in equipment support for China Coast Guard vessels, this paper presents a systematic review of research progress in ship fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) systems based on large language models (LLMs). Shipboard environments pose unique challenges, including weak communication links at sea, limited onboard computational resources, high levels of mechanical noise, and stringent reliability requirements for safety-critical systems. Traditional datadriven FDD methods, while leveraging accumulated industrial IoT data, suffer from a scarcity of high-quality labeled data and limited cross-scenario generalization capability. LLMs offer new opportunities due to their capabilities in multi-modal understanding, knowledge fusion, and zero-shot or few-shot reasoning. ［Method］A systematic literature review methodology was adopted to analyze 95 relevant publications from 2022 to 2026. The search was conducted across Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and CNKI databases using keyword combinations including "fault diagnosis", "fault detection", "large language model", "LLM", "GPT", "PHM", "intelligent operation and maintenance", and "agent". After initial screening of titles and abstracts, followed by backward snowballing, 95 papers were ultimately included for analysis. LLM opti mization strategies in industrial FDD were summarized into four dimensions: input-side enhancement (including RAG, knowledge graphs, multi-modal LLMs, and digital twins), model-side optimization (including finetuning or retraining, prompt engineering, and multi-model collaboration), output-side refinement (feedback optimization), and architectural design (integrating LLMs with signal processing, machine learning, neural networks, and multi-agent systems). In response to the characteristics of shipboard data heterogeneity, limited computational resources, and stringent reliability requirements, a hierarchical, decoupled, multi-agent collaborative reference architecture for shipboard FDD systems is proposed. The architecture consists of five layers from top to bottom: the interaction layer (supporting multi-modal input and adaptive output), the agent layer (comprising eight specialized agents for reception, scheduling, query, process management, reasoning, generation, data processing, and feedback), the model layer (including a domain-specific fine-tuned LLM, an embedding model, and a lightweight multi-modal model), the tool layer (featuring time-series signal processing with dual pipelines for feature extraction and semantic mapping, along with text processing, vector embedding, multi-modal alignment, and knowledge graph tools), and the data layer (containing a raw database, a vector knowledge base, and a knowledge graph).［Results］The number of research publications on LLMs in the industrial FDD field increased from 4 in 2023 to 22 in 2024, and further surged to 61 in 2025, with approximately 76% focusing on input-side enhancement and model-side optimization. This trend indicates rapidly growing research interest and the significant potential of LLMs in this domain. For shipboard scenarios, the proposed architecture supports localized deployment of lightweight LLMs through quantization and pruning techniques, enabling multi-source data fusion via vector knowledge bases and knowledge graphs. Based on multi-agent collaboration, it enables automatic task decomposition for fault diagnosis and closed-loop decision-making. The architecture also incorporates mechanisms for uncertainty-aware conflict resolution (including historical accuracy-based confidence calibration, external hard-constraint anchoring, and conservative decision strategies), multi-agent overhead optimization (on-demand activation, hierarchical context management, agent role consolidation, and asynchronous task scheduling), and adaptation to unknown faults (zero-shot reasoning with LLM prior knowledge, cross-device fault pattern transfer, active learning with human-in-the-loop annotation, and synthetic data augmentation).［Conclusion］The proposed hierarchical reference architecture provides a feasible pathway and framework for transforming shipboard FDD systems toward an intelligent paradigm driven by the synergy of data and knowledge. Future research should focus on trustworthy outputs, adaptive capabilities, and system integration to enhance equipment support efficiency and navigation safety. Key future directions include robust intelligence under strong constraints (multi-modal signal characterization under highnoise conditions, and LLM decision trustworthiness assessment compliant with IEC 61508 functional safety requirements), continuous self-adaptation in offline environments (ontological incremental learning and knowledge distillation during communication blackouts, and few-shot or zero-shot cross-device fault transfer diagnosis), and system integration with standardization (standardized interfaces with existing ship cyberphysical systems, and verification and validation methods compliant with China Classification Society specifications). © 2026, Editorial Department of Chinese Journal of Ship Research. Title: Wildfire digital twins: a paradigm shift from monitoring systems to intelligent decision infrastructures

Abstract: Wildfires are becoming more frequent, severe, and complex driven by global warming and climate change, posing escalating threats to ecosystems, infrastructure, public health, and community safety worldwide. Recent advances in Earth observation, artificial intelligence, physics-based modelling, and cyberinfrastructure have accelerated the development of wildfire digital twins (WFDTs), yet existing capabilities remain fragmented across monitoring, fusion, prediction, simulation, and decision support. Unlike prior reviews that primarily address individual aspect of wildfire, this review and vision paper provides an integrated synthesis of WFDTs. We propose a six-layer WFDT architecture, identify six core capabilities spanning situational awareness through adaptive learning, and organise applications across the wildfire lifecycle from prevention and detection to response, smoke management, and post-fire recovery. Building upon these advances, we outline a research roadmap toward autonomous WFDTs through advances in hybrid intelligence, trustworthy AI, uncertainty quantification, decision intelligence, and continual learning. We envision that the defining characteristic of future WFDTs is not increasingly realistic digital representation, but their evolution into a new paradigm that continuously integrates sensing, prediction, uncertainty quantification, optimisation, governance, and human expertise towards a paradigm of intelligent, trustworthy decision infrastructures that continuously support human-centred wildfire decision making. © 2026 The Author(s). Abstract: Smart polymer composite actuators are emerging as enabling materials for next-generation soft robotics by combining mechanical compliance, multifunctionality, and programmable responsiveness within lightweight architectures. Their ability to convert electrical, thermal, magnetic, optical, and chemical stimuli into controlled deformation provides advantages for adaptive interaction with complex environments. Advances in three-dimensional (3D) and four-dimensional (4D) printing have expanded their design space through multimaterial integration, spatially programmed architectures, functional gradients, and time-dependent shape transformation. Concurrently, machine learning (ML) offers new opportunities for material discovery, structure–property prediction, fabrication optimization, actuator modeling, inverse design, sensing, and intelligent control. This review critically examines the integration of polymer composites, 3D/4D printing, computational modeling, and ML across the materials-to-device development chain, from formulation and architecture to manufacturing, actuation, sensing, control, and lifecycle monitoring. Particular attention is given to printability–functionality trade-offs, multimaterial interfaces, manufacturing scalability and reproducibility, dataset limitations, uncertainty, simulation-to-reality transfer, and model generalization. Emerging strategies, including physics-informed ML, multiscale density functional theory–molecular dynamics–ML frameworks, digital twins, closed-loop design–print–test optimization, and sustainable composite systems, are discussed as pathways toward more predictive and efficient development. The review emphasizes that high ML accuracy does not necessarily ensure transferability or reliable physical performance and highlights the need for standardized validation and experimentally grounded models. Finally, opportunities for increasingly autonomous, self-adaptive, and closed-loop soft robotic systems are outlined, providing a roadmap toward reliable, scalable, sustainable, and application-ready intelligent soft robotic technologies. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Abstract: Dynamic inductive charging (DIC) combined with hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities offers a promising pathway toward extended-range electric vehicles with grid integration benefits. However, real-time optimal energy management remains challenging due to multi-axis coil misalignment, component aging, and bidirectional power flow uncertainty. This paper proposes an adaptive digital twin driven artificial intelligence (AI) energy management framework integrating physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), soft actor critic (SAC) deep reinforcement learning, and model predictive control (MPC) for optimal power distribution among a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC), lithium-ion battery, supercapacitor, dynamic wireless charging, and grid interface in four-wheel drive electric vehicles (4WD-EVs). The framework features: (1) a self-evolving digital twin with online learning via Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) updating every 50 cycles; (2) a PINN-based state estimator for battery-state estimation, with an average inference time of 1.1 ms and a worst-case latency of 2.8 ms; (3) a hierarchical SAC–MPC strategy with high-level mode selection and low-level power optimization; (4) real-time five-degree-of-freedom WPT misalignment compensation, achieving a mean efficiency of 91.5% under the evaluated dynamic lateral misalignment conditions, with a 50 mm displacement amplitude; (5) degradation-aware V2G optimization generating €582.50/year in revenue while reducing battery aging by 31.8%; and (6) comprehensive techno-economic analysis yielding a discounted payback period of approximately 5.57 years and a net present value of approximately €3777 over a 10-year horizon. Validated through 200+ hours of hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation on the dSPACE/NVIDIA Jetson platform, the proposed approach achieves a 24.3% cost reduction and 31.8% lower battery degradation. The MPC controller exhibits an average execution time of 32.1 ms, a 95th-percentile latency of 44.8 ms, and a worst-case latency of 62.4 ms, while remaining within the 100-ms real-time control deadline. Results demonstrate the viability of adaptive digital twins for next-generation EVs with autonomous charging and multi-source architectures. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Advanced Analytics and Machine Learning for Strategic Insights: Technological Evolution and Social Transformation in the Era of Industrial and Social 5.0

Affiliations: Quantum Serbia, Serbia; Serbian AI Association, Serbia
Authors with affiliations: Ivković J., Quantum Serbia, Serbia, Serbian AI Association, Serbia
Abstract: How do data become social capital – more than a corporate asset, a measurable public good that improves health, equity, and sustainability? This chapter answers across four arcs. First, it tracks the analytic stack from OLAP and data mining to Big Data, Deep Learning (DL), and causal, privacy-preserving pipelines, marking the shift from hindsight to intervention. Second, it frames Society 5.0 as human-centred by design: explainability, fairness, and documented governance as operating requirements within edge–core architectures which keep people in the loop. Third, it examines substrates which make real-time analytics feasible at acceptable cost: neuromorphic spiking networks at the edge, photonic linear layers for matrix-heavy inference, and quantum-assisted routines where structure and noise budgets permit – judged by energy per decision, latency, and audit trails rather than headline FLOPS. Finally, applications ground the argument: clinical CNNs, legal Natural Language Processing (NLP), federated learning (FL) for data sovereignty, SHAP for recourse, and physics-informed digital twins which enable therapy planning before intervention. Organoid intelligence (OI) is treated with scientific caution – as exploratory, protocol-sensitive co-processing. The result is a pragmatic roadmap: align models with social outcomes, measure uncertainty and energy, document decisions, and preserve agency – so analytics functions as a civic capability in Society 5.0. © 2027 selection and editorial matter, Amarnath Padhi, Sabyasachi Rath, Elena Gurgu, and Dac-Nhuong Le; individual chapters, the contributors.

Abstract: Digital twin (DT) technology is emerging as a key enabler for data driven decision making in agriculture. The development of high fidelity agricultural DTs is hindered by a central paradox: the data streams that are used to power DT systems are born with quality deficiencies. While the literature has addressed the technology architecture of agricultural DTs and the application opportunities of agricultural DTs, the poor data quality has been treated as a peripheral issue. The review shows that the quality of data is mysteriously uncertain because of intrinsic bottlenecks associated with the physical acquisition and representation of data, social and technical barriers to data integration and management that amplify data quality uncertainties, and the propagation of data quality uncertainties throughout the DT pipeline to undermine the model outputs and provides decision support to users. To address the issues, the review will postulate a multi-layered governance framework and critique emerging technology pathways regarding AI-cleaning and augmenting data, cloud-edge-terminal collaborative architectures for real-time processing of data, trusted traceability using distributed ledger technology, and dynamic model/data fusion. In conclusion, the development of the intelligent and sustainable production of food will be achieved through a pathway that integrates domain knowledge with artificial intelligence. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to The Brazilian Society of Mechanical Sciences and Engineering 2026.

Title: AI-Driven Agent-Based Urban Digital Twins: A Systematic Literature Review
Affiliations: Technical University of Denmark, Dynamical Systems, Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, Kongens Lyngby, 2800, Denmark; Abertay University, Department of Games Technology and Mathematics, Dundee, DD1 1HG, United Kingdom

Abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) and agent-based approaches to support intelligent and autonomous urban systems. However, existing reviews largely examine DTs, AI techniques, or agent-based approaches separately, leaving limited insight into how these dimensions interact and how such systems progress toward higher levels of intelligence and real-world deployment. This systematic literature review (SLR) analyzes 82 primary research studies describing AI-driven agent-based approaches in urban digital twins as a system of systems and found in four major scientific databases, i.e. IEEE Xplore, Scopus, Web of Science, and ACM Digital Library. The selected studies were systematically examined with respect to digital twin types, AI techniques used, agent type, agent roles, maturity level, application domains, and key challenges. As a result, we categorize digital twins into five types: conceptual DT, descriptive DT, predictive DT, prescriptive DT and autonomous DT, with the most frequent being the predictive DT. Reinforcement learning emerged as the most common AI technique, while the hierarchical agent taxonomy shows that multi-agent systems dominate at the architectural level, and decision-making and acting is the main role of agents, followed by control. We also identified that most studies remain at relatively low Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) and rely predominantly on simulation-based or conceptual validation, revealing a substantial gap between technological advancement and real-world deployment. The analysis further shows that implementation challenges evolve across the DT life-cycle. Moreover, we found that only a limited proportion of studies explicitly address uncertainty, while the majority rely on deterministic or idealized assumptions. Our analysis further revealed that most urban digital twin systems are in the early stages of development, and we identified key research gaps and, based on this, suggested future research directions. Overall, this SLR provides a structured synthesis of AI-driven agent-based urban digital twins and identifies priorities for interoperability, standardized evaluation, real-world validation, and scalable autonomous urban systems.  © 2013 IEEE.

Title: Autonomous Robotaxi Docking Using Digital Twin Vision and LiDAR Planning
Source title: 2026 International Conference on Green Technologies and Sustainable Solutions, GTSS 2026
Affiliations: OH, United States; MI, United States; CA, United States
Authors with affiliations: Sucharitha R.S., OH, United States; Sanikal V., MI, United States; Choudhary R., CA, United States; Pradhan S., MI, United States
Abstract: Autonomous robotaxi fleets need a reliable way to charge without human help. For this to work, the charging process must be fully automated. Robotic charging is more demanding than ordinary autonomous parking. The vehicle has to align precisely with a fixed charging interface. The system also depends on accurate perception, motion planning, and manipulator reachability. This study presents a digital-twin-based approach for automated charging. The setup uses both camera and LiDAR sensors. These sensors guide a robotic arm as it connects to the vehicle. The framework includes vehicle-motion planning, charging-port detection, and pose estimation that accounts for uncertainty. A digital twin of the charging station provides key information. It includes charger geometry, docking points, safety zones, and regions with higher uncertainty. The vehicle must reach a suitable docking position so the manipulator can operate within limited pose errors. This requirement defines a docking-constrained task. The system is tested in a CARLA simulation environment. The simulation includes dynamic agents and sensor noise. Results show that planning with docking semantics and uncertainty improves first-attempt connection success. It also reduces the need for late-stage replanning when compared with navigation-focused baselines. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: A Digital-Twin-Driven Framework for Traffic and Energy Management Leveraging Generative AI
Source title: 2026 5th MEC International Conference on Advanced Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Smart Cities, ICADAAI 2026
Affiliations: Indira Gandhi University, Dept. of Cse, Meerpur, Rewari, India; Middle East College, Dept. of Computing and Electronic Engg., Oman
Authors with affiliations: Yadav D., Indira Gandhi University, Dept. of Cse, Meerpur, Rewari, India; Sheoran S., Indira Gandhi University, Dept. of Cse, Meerpur, Rewari, India; Pandey J., Middle East College, Dept. of Computing and Electronic Engg., Oman; Yadav N., Indira Gandhi University, Dept. of Cse, Meerpur, Rewari, India
Abstract: With urbanisation, pressures in urban areas and the pressure of climate are increasing, cities may need smart and data-based decision making by implementing intelligent operations and strategic action architectures. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a revolution in smart city management with the potential to generate such data, perform urban analysis and consider policy alternatives, among other things, when there is an uncertainty. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are the latest generation of urban analytics such as models for generating scenarios and understanding semantic analysis, with diffusion models and large language models (LLMs). Generative models should not be part of decisions, but instead can be used as one end with UDTs and optimization pipeline and integrated within our city decision-support (CDA) architecture. We propose that the next generation is a general model for such a unified model, based on both the global and a customized algorithm based across cities that combines spatio-temporal and digital twin problem modelling methods and models together and provide multivariable approach in urban decision-making from multiple dimensions. We model the framework in traffic signal control and energy demand response tasks on calibrated synthetic cities' urban data. The spatio-temporal GAN (ST-GAN) and conditional VAE (cVAE) are trained and compared to standard deterministic LSTM and Gaussian process baselines based on both the prediction and quality metrics (RMSE, DTW and coverage) for the performance (expected delay, peak-to-average ratio and worst-case load). We conducted our experiments and showed that GenAI-based decision pipelines significantly outperform traditional baselines for predictive accuracy as well as case diversity and decision robustness in real world smart city data. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The recent developments in data-driven methods have paved the way for new methodologies to provide accurate and robust full state reconstruction of engineering systems under any operating conditions. Such approaches can be attractive for next-generation nuclear reactors, which represent particularly challenging applications for sensing and monitoring due to the complexity of the strongly coupled physics involved and the extremely harsh environments. Data-driven techniques can combine different sources of information, including computational proxy models and noisy measurements on the system, to robustly estimate the state. This work leverages the novel Shallow Recurrent Decoder (SHRED) architecture to infer the entire state vector (both neutronics and fluid dynamics fields) of a circulating fuel reactor, the Molten Salt Fast Reactor. The standard architecture is extended to treat parametric time-series data, ensuring the possibility of investigating different scenarios and showing its capabilities to provide an accurate state estimation in various conditions. The proposed methodology adopts possible innovative sensing strategies in new-generation reactors, including out-of-core time-series neutron flux measurements alone, in-core sensing measuring the precursor concentrations or mobile probes advected by the fuel flow. The promising results of this work are further strengthened by the possibility of quantifying the uncertainty associated with the state estimation due to the considerably low training cost of the architecture. The ability of SHRED to deliver real-time, system-wide reconstruction highlights its potential for reactor monitoring, control, and digital twin development in next-generation circulating fuel systems. © 2026 The Author(s). Abstract: The rapid development of Electric Vehicle (EV) has increased the demand for battery management systems (BMSs) capable of ensuring safe, reliable, and efficient operation under dynamic conditions. This review critically examines the evolution of EV-BMS technologies from conventional monitoring and protection to AI-enabled, connected, and application-oriented systems. Unlike reviews that primarily address individual BMS functions or specific battery technologies, this work integrates battery characteristics and degradation with state estimation, thermal management, cell balancing, fault diagnosis, safety, and emerging BMS architectures, while emphasizing their interactions and practical deployment constraints. Recent developments in machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, physics-informed methods, cloud-assisted and digital-twin-based BMS, wireless communication, cybersecurity, and emerging battery chemistries are comparatively examined in terms of computational burden, data requirements, safety, scalability, and real-time applicability. The review further identifies system-level challenges related to cross-chemistry transferability, uncertainty and sensor faults, AI validation, communication reliability, cloud-edge coordination, and BMS adaptation for emerging and second-life batteries. These findings highlight the need to move beyond isolated algorithmic improvements toward validated, interoperable, and application-aware BMS architectures for future EVs. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: AI4Land: A Scalable Deep Learning Framework on MareNostrum5 for Global High-Resolution Land Use Reconstruction

Abstract: Uncertainty in the terrestrial carbon cycle remains a major constraint in climate projections, partly driven by the uncertainties affecting the land surface representation and variability in Earth system models. To address this limitation, we present a data-driven framework - AI4Land - for generating high-resolution historical reconstructions and future projections of key land surface variables. The framework follows a two-phase approach using a U-Net architecture. In the first phase, which is the focus of this work, it reconstructs annual land use and land cover by integrating coarse-resolution scenario data with static geophysical features. In a planned second phase, the resulting high-resolution maps will be used to predict dynamic biophysical variables, particularly leaf area index, at finer temporal scales. Trained on Earth observation data, the models learn to reproduce spatially explicit and physically consistent land surface patterns, extending temporal coverage to periods lacking direct observations. AI4Land was developed and trained on MareNostrum5, demonstrating how GPU-accelerated HPC infrastructure enables global-scale climate AI pipelines. The final product is a suite of open-source emulators designed for real-time coupling with digital twin platforms, such as those developed under the Destination Earth initiative. By delivering realistic and evolving land surface conditions on demand, this work aims to reduce critical uncertainties and improve the predictive power of next-generation climate simulations. 2026 The Authors. Abstract: Bluff-body flows combine early separation, coherent wake organization, vortex shedding, and strong sensitivity to geometry, Reynolds number, inflow condition, and three-dimensional transition. These features make them both canonical fluid-mechanics benchmarks and demanding targets for neural-network-based modeling. This review provides a representative, physics-oriented synthesis of neural-network approaches for bluff-body flows. Instead of organizing the field by architecture or prediction task, the review asks which wake mechanisms current models represent and which validation evidence makes those claims trustworthy. It examines how current models represent separation, wake topology, pressure-wake coupling, coherent shedding, turbulence statistics, closure behavior, and flow-control mechanisms. We discuss data sources, flow representations, model classes, validation practices, and practical uses in surrogate prediction, reconstruction, monitoring, control, and digital-twin-type workflows. The review emphasizes that low numerical error by itself does not establish physical learning, and argues for validation based on topology, spectra, force response, uncertainty, generalization, and interpretable mechanism evidence. © 2026 Author(s).

Title: Digital and bioinspired approaches to designing sustainable educational spaces: Modeling, optimization, and adaptive systems
Affiliations: Department, S. Seifullin Kazakh Agrotechnical Research University, Kazakhstan
Authors with affiliations: Anafina A., Department, S. Seifullin Kazakh Agrotechnical Research University, Kazakhstan; Kornilova A., Department, S. Seifullin Kazakh Agrotechnical Research University, Kazakhstan
Abstract: This study presents a mathematically rigorous, digitally bio-inspired framework for sustainable educational space design. Integrating parametric Building Information Modeling (BIM), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), surrogate response modeling, bio-inspired multi-objective optimization, and interval type-2 fuzzy adaptive control, the methodology is applied to a prototypical 4,860 m² learning center governed by fifteen decision variables. The optimization formulation simultaneously minimizes energy use intensity, discomfort hours, operational carbon, acoustic penalty, and daylight deficiency while maximizing graph-based spatial flexibility. Evaluating genetic algorithms, self-adaptive particle swarm optimization (SAPSO), and ant colony optimization across hypervolume and composite sustainability indices, SAPSO proved optimal. It reduced energy use intensity from 154.2 to 93.7 kWh/m²·yr, operational carbon from 127.8 to 75.4 kgCO₂e/m²·yr, thermal discomfort from 418 to 143 h/yr, and reverberation time from 0.92 to 0.59 s, while boosting useful daylight illuminance from 54% to 81%. Additionally, interval type-2 fuzzy control yielded a further 17.6% in daily energy savings over rule-based operations. Architecturally interpreted through spatial typology, circulation, acoustic privacy, and user experience, the mathematical engine directly informs spatial design without supplanting human architectural judgment. © The Author 2026.

Title: Quantum-Inspired Graph Neural Digital Twins for the sub-microsecond topological co-design and temporal degradation modeling of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin smart gels
Affiliations: Bajpai & Co. Research Private Limited (Bajpai Labs), Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow, India
Authors with affiliations: Bajpai K., Bajpai & Co. Research Private Limited (Bajpai Labs), Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow, India
Abstract: The clinical translation of lignocellulosic smart gels is constrained by empirical formulation screening, complex structure–property relationships, and uncertainty in degradation and therapeutic-release behavior. This study aims to determine whether a unified computational digital-twin framework can (i) optimize the crosslinking topology of cellulose-, hemicellulose-, and lignin-based matrices, (ii) predict their mechanical and temporal degradation behavior, and (iii) translate optimized formulations into real-time control parameters for microfluidic synthesis. To address these objectives, we develop a Quantum-Inspired Graph Neural Digital Twin (Q-GNDT) that represents molecular interactions as dynamic non-Euclidean graphs and formulates topological optimization as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. A temporal graph-decay model couples pH-dependent hydrolysis, enzymatic cleavage, percolation loss, and drug diffusion to predict time-resolved degradation and release. The computational architecture is integrated with an edge-AI control model designed for sub-microsecond microfluidic actuation. Retrospective cross-validation against published experimental datasets from three independent studies yielded mean absolute errors of 2.1% for pore size, 2.9% for storage modulus, and 1.5% for drug-release kinetics, with an overall RMSE of 0.74%. An in-silico targeted-delivery case study further produced 4.1% initial burst release, 98.0% cumulative delivery, and near-linear release kinetics (R2 = 0.991). These results indicate that Q-GNDT can serve as a computational design and screening framework for narrowing the experimental search space of programmable lignocellulosic biomaterials. Prospective synthesis, biological testing, and in vivo validation remain necessary before clinical translation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Authors: Benbouzid M.

Title: Large language models, ChatGPT, and beyond: A new paradigm for condition monitoring and prognosis in power and energy systems
Affiliations: University of Brest, UMR CNRS 6027 IRDL, Brest, France
Authors with affiliations: Benbouzid M., University of Brest, UMR CNRS 6027 IRDL, Brest, France
Abstract: Large language models and related foundation models offer new capabilities for interpreting heterogeneous information, retrieving engineering knowledge, and supporting high-level decision processes in power and energy systems. This Perspective examines their role in condition monitoring and prognostics and health management, with particular emphasis on remaining useful life estimation. To support language and multimodal model interpretation of structured and validated estimates, we propose a digital twin-centric architecture comprising physics-guided hybrid estimation, digital twin synchronization, rule-governed semantic translation, foundation model reasoning, output validation, and human supervision. The specific contribution is threefold. First, the proposed layering principle distinguishes physically consistent estimation, system integration, and higher-level reasoning functions. Second, an auditable semantic interface is defined to encode health indicators, degradation states, remaining useful life distributions, uncertainty information, operating context, provenance, retrieved evidence, and permitted reasoning scope. Third, a deployment-oriented reliability framework relates physical consistency, digital twin consistency, explanation fidelity, uncertainty preservation, robustness, traceability, safe deferral, latency, data sensitivity, and computational requirements to edge, on premises, cloud, and hybrid implementations. An illustrative battery state-of-health and remaining useful life use case demonstrates the resulting information flow. The foundation model layer is primarily intended for slow-timescale, human-supervised functions such as diagnostic explanation, degradation interpretation, maintenance prioritization, inspection planning, and fleet-level assessment, rather than protection or real-time control. The Perspective also examines complementary roles for small language models, tiny recursive models, world models, large language models, and multimodal foundation models and identifies priorities for their reliable evaluation and deployment in power and energy prognostics and health management. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Digital twin-driven hybrid fuzzy Bayesian simulation framework for dynamic green credit risk assessment in manufacturing enterprises
Source title: International Journal of Modeling, Simulation, and Scientific Computing
Affiliations: Hunan International Economics University, Business School, Changsha, Hunan, 410205, China
Authors with affiliations: Yang N., Hunan International Economics University, Business School, Changsha, Hunan, 410205, China
Abstract: Green credit risk assessment for manufacturing enterprises is a dynamic and complex problem affected by operational states, environmental uncertainty, financial conditions, information quality, and interactive risk evolution. Traditional assessment methods depend heavily on low-frequency financial and disclosure data and therefore have limited ability to capture early risk signals arising from production operations, energy consumption, environmental performance, and supply-chain disturbances. In addition, conventional machine-learning models provide limited interpretability for causal dependence and uncertain risk propagation. This paper proposes a digital twin-driven hybrid fuzzy dynamic Bayesian network (DT-FDBN) framework for dynamic green credit risk assessment and scenario simulation in manufacturing enterprises. The framework integrates multi-source information covering financial solvency, production and equipment operation, energy consumption and emissions, green transition, environmental disclosure and information credibility, and the external environment into a unified enterprise digital-twin representation. Fuzzy evidence transformation is used to represent incomplete and imprecise observations, while credibility correction and group-level sensor reliability reduce the influence of unreliable digital-twin evidence. The DT-FDBN further models hierarchical risk dependence, temporal evolution, and probabilistic uncertainty propagation, supporting dynamic inference, key-factor diagnosis, multi-period prediction, and intervention-scenario simulation. Based on a semi-synthetic dataset containing 2160 enterprise-month observations from 60 manufacturing enterprises, the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 0.881, recall of 0.893, (Formula presented)-score of 0.869, AUC of 0.943, and Brier score of 0.079. It outperforms XGBoost and conventional fuzzy dynamic Bayesian networks in overall predictive and calibration performance and identifies operational and environmental deterioration earlier than financial-only assessment. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and dynamically adaptive modeling paradigm for manufacturing green credit risk management. © The Author(s) 2026

Abstract: Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries combine a high theoretical specific energy with low-cost active materials, yet their development remains constrained by coupled reaction pathways, mobile intermediates, lithium-metal instability, and a large design space that changes with loading, electrolyte inventory, temperature, format, and cycling history. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a way to connect these variables, but most published demonstrations remain isolated within small computational datasets, literature-derived tables, or single-laboratory cell series. This review develops an evidence-first, closed-loop framework for AI-enabled Li–S research that links observation, learning, decision, validation, and model updating. It critically examines data infrastructure, text and multimodal extraction, descriptor learning, catalyst and electrolyte design, physics-informed state inference, degradation prognosis, autonomous experimentation, and digital twins. The available evidence shows that machine learning (ML) can compress high-dimensional calculations, recover useful structure–property relations, and predict selected cell outcomes within bounded domains. However, ML has not yet demonstrated robust transfer across laboratories, cell formats, or practical operating conditions. The main barriers are incomplete metadata, non-independent data splits, uncertain labels, weak uncertainty calibration, and limited prospective validation. To address these gaps, the review introduces a minimum data schema, an evidence-fidelity pathway that separates proxy prediction from decision-grade evidence, task-specific benchmarking requirements, and a minimum viable digital-twin architecture for Li–S cells. The central conclusion is that AI becomes decision-grade only when its predictions are physically credible, uncertainty-aware, experimentally actionable, and iteratively validated. © 2026 The Authors.
